Erasmus MC
Department of Radiology
Date: 15 January 2025
Exam: mpMRI Prostate (3T)

Clinical indication: Elevated PSA 4.53 ng/mL, prior biopsy Gleason 3+3. Assess for focal lesion.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume is 41.0 mL. The transition zone is unremarkable. In the peripheral zone, right posterolateral aspect, there is a focal lesion measuring approximately 12 mm in maximal diameter. This area demonstrates markedly restricted diffusion on DWI (b=1400), corresponding to a hypointense area on the apparent diffusion coefficient map. On T2-weighted imaging, the lesion appears as a distinct hypointense region. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences show early and intense focal enhancement. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified. No suspicious pelvic lymphadenopathy.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone.
PSA density 0.12 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage cT1c.
csPCa predicted probability 0.84312165.

previous_notes.author: Dr. F. de Boer (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with incidentally elevated PSA of 2.5 ng/mL. Digital rectal examination was unremarkable. Given the PSA level and age, a transrectal ultrasound-guided systematic biopsy was performed. Pathology returned showing Gleason 3+3, ISUP grade group 1, with noted cribriform pattern and IDC-P. Patient was informed of the findings and the presence of high-risk features. Active surveillance was discussed, but the patient expressed anxiety regarding the high-risk patterns and requested a second opinion on management options. Referred to urology for further evaluation and discussion of treatment pathways.
